Chapter 6: The Writing on the Wall—Lessons Left Behind.
Sometimes, the most powerful guidance doesn’t come from long speeches or dramatic moments.
Instead, it shows up in the simplest words, scribbled down in a flash of clarity.
Picture this: as the little person made his way through the maze, he often stopped to jot down what he’d learned, right there on the walls.
These messages weren’t just for him—they were meant for anyone who might come after, anyone who could be feeling lost or scared.
He wrote things like, “Change happens—expect it,” and, “Move with the cheese and enjoy it!”
At first, those words might seem almost too simple, right? But as he kept walking, he realized just how easy it is to forget them—especially when fear starts to creep in.
Writing them down turned into his anchor, a way to hold on to what really mattered whenever uncertainty showed up.
Back in the real world, the friends who’d gathered to share their stories found themselves thinking about these “writings on the wall.”
One friend remembered a time when sudden changes at work left her feeling completely off balance. She’d held on to her old routines, hoping things would just go back to normal.
But it wasn’t until she accepted the new reality—and allowed herself to adapt—that she finally found her footing.
Another friend thought back to a painful breakup. At first, he resisted moving on, hoping things might somehow return to how they were.
But once he shifted his focus to what he could learn from the experience, things started to get a little easier.
It became clear that these simple reminders could really guide them through tough times.
Most people, when faced with change, forget the basics: pay attention to what’s happening, let go of what’s gone, and keep moving forward.
Those writings on the wall weren’t just advice—they were lifelines, helping people find their way when the road ahead felt uncertain.
The friends realized something powerful: everyone leaves their own “writings” behind.
Whether it’s a small act of courage, a few encouraging words, or a lesson learned the hard way, these moments become part of the invisible map that helps others find their way through their own mazes.
